extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer algebra system (computational group theorists, mathematicians, and advanced students working with groups)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference guidance for computing and manipulating conjugacy classes, subgroup classes, class maps, power maps, class matrices, subgroup posets, normal subgroups, and characters in the Magma system, including algorithms, parameters, and efficiency notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConjugate(G, x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x and y are elements of a group G, IsConjugate(G, x, y) tests whether x and y are conjugate in G. If x and y are conjugate, the function returns as its second value an element g such that x^g = y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown; use when testing a (small) number of individual conjugacy relations. For identifying classes of many elements, consider ClassMap for efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class(H, x) / Conjugates(H, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of conjugates of x under the action of the subgroup H is given by Class(H, x) or Conjugates(H, x). If H is G, the function returns the entire conjugacy class of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions return the class as an enumerated set and therefore should not be used on large classes; to get the size of the class more efficiently use Index(G, Centralizer(G, x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes(G) / ConjugacyClasses(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs all the conjugacy classes of G. Returns a sequence of tuples; each tuple contains the order of elements in that class, the length (cardinality) of the class, and a representative element for the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The returned sequence is designed for easy computation of classes if desired; a special display format is provided when printed. Individual tuple components are accessed in the usual way (e.g. cubecl[9], cubecl[9][2], cubecl[4,1]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes: algorithm selection (Al parameter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classes function accepts an Al parameter to select the algorithm used to determine conjugacy classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Al = "Action" finds classes by computing orbits under conjugation (useful for small groups). Al = "Random" uses a random algorithm attempting to locate an element in each class. Al = "Extension" employs an inductive algorithm using a sequence of larger quotients determined by an elementary abelian series. Choose based on group size and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: AssertAttribute to set known classes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the user already knows a set of representatives for the classes, AssertAttribute may be used to define a value for the "Classes" attribute for the group by providing exactly one representative from each conjugacy class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to avoid recomputing classes when a reliable representative set is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassMap(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates the class map f : G → R where R is the sequence of class representatives; f(x) = index of the representative for the class containing x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ClassMap precomputes additional information to speed up class identification; if classes are not yet known they will be computed. The returned mapping can be applied to individual elements, sets, and sequences for fast bulk classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassRepresentative(G, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the class representative of x, i.e., the representative for the class containing x that appears in the sequence returned by Classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent lookups may be performed via the Classes sequence; ClassRepresentative is convenient shorthand.

rubrics_metrics.name: PowerMap(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates the powermap φ which records the behaviour of conjugacy classes under taking powers: φ : C × {1..e} → C where φ(i, t) is the index of the class containing x_i^t (x_i a representative of class Ki).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the class map is not already known, PowerMap will cause it to be created. Use to inspect images of classes under particular powers (squares, cubes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassMatrix(G, i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the structure constant matrix M_i for class i: the (j,k)-entry c_{ijk} is the number of solutions (x,y) to xy = z with z fixed in class K_k, x in K_i, y in K_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation examples provided; use to study multiplication of class sums and structure constants of the centre of the group algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubgroupClasses(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines a representative subgroup for each conjugacy class of subgroups of G. Returns a sequence of records; each record contains at least the fields 'subgroup', 'order', and 'length', and optionally 'presentation' (for permutation groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical only for groups of moderate order or with relatively few subgroup classes. Returned sequence allows iteration and extraction of subgroup information (e.g., orders, representatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction parameters for subgroup functions (OrderEqual, OrderDividing, IsNormal, IsRegular)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subgroup construction functions accept parameters to restrict the kinds of subgroups constructed: OrderEqual (integer n) -> only construct subgroups of order n; OrderDividing (integer n) -> only construct subgroups with order dividing n; IsNormal (true) -> only normal subgroups; IsRegular (true) -> only regular subgroups (permutation groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These parameters apply to all subgroup functions including SubgroupClasses and can drastically reduce computation by narrowing the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Varieties of subgroup functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized functions exist to construct particular varieties of subgroups: ElementaryAbelianSubgroups(G), AbelianSubgroups(G), SolubleSubgroups(G), NilpotentSubgroups(G), PerfectSubgroups(G), SimpleSubgroups(G), RegularSubgroups(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate specialized function when interested only in subgroups of a given structural type (example showed ElementaryAbelianSubgroups with OrderEqual parameter).

rubrics_metrics.name: SubgroupLattice(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines conjugacy classes of subgroups and builds the poset (lattice) L of subgroup classes where edges join classes if a subgroup of one class is a maximal subgroup of a subgroup of the other class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of the poset can be very time-consuming; use with care. Boolean parameters: Properties (record abstract properties of each subgroup), Centralizers (record classes of centralizers), Normalizers (record classes of normalizers); defaults are false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poset operations and extraction (Number of classes, L!i, Bottom(L), Top(L), L!H, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard operations on subgroup posets: #L (number of conjugacy classes), L!i (ith element/class), Z!i (coercion to poset element), L!H (poset element containing subgroup H), Bottom(L) (trivial class), Top(L) (class of G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the standard relational ops eq, ne, ge, gt, le, lt to compare poset elements. Iteration and chain construction examples are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracting subgroup-poset information (Group, Centralizer, Normalizer, Length, Order, MaximalSubgroups, MinimalOvergroups, NumberOfInclusions, Representative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions to extract data from a poset element e: Group(e) returns representative subgroup; Centralizer(e,f) returns class containing centralizers of a fixed representative of f in e; Normalizer(e,f); Length(e) number of subgroups in class; Order(e) order of subgroups in class; MaximalSubgroups(e); MinimalOvergroups(e,f); NumberOfInclusions(e,f); Representative(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to explore containment, normalizers, centralizers and maximal/minimal relations in the lattice. Examples illustrate retrieving class orders and maximal-subgroup relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintBurnsideMatrix(L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints the Burnside matrix of a subgroup poset L: matrix (b_{ij}) where b_{ij} is the number of subgroups in class S_i which either contain r_j or are contained in r_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Burnside matrix displays containment relationships between all pairs of conjugacy classes of subgroups; useful in combinatorial and enumerative investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NormalSubgroups(G) and MinimalNormalSubgroups(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: NormalSubgroups(G) returns the normal subgroups of G as a sequence of records (same format as SubgroupClasses). MinimalNormalSubgroups(G) finds minimal normal subgroups (efficient for primitive permutation groups, naive otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current techniques are limited to groups of moderate order; examples show usage and returned orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassFunctionSpace(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates the space W of class functions on G as a k-dimensional vector space over an appropriate cyclotomic field (k = number of conjugacy classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This function will create the conjugacy classes of G but will not compute irreducible characters. Use this space to build class functions and manipulate them algebraically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing individual class functions / characters (elt< W | ... >, W!Q, Character flag)
rubrics_metrics.description: A class function (a1,...,ak) may be created by elt< W | a1, ..., ak > or W!Q (Q a list). A Boolean parameter Character on the elt-constructor may be used to flag a as a character: elt< W | a1, ... , ak : Character := true >.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the irreducible characters of G are known it is not possible to determine whether a is actually a character; use the Character flag only when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacterRing(G) and representing characters
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterRing(G) provides a convenient ring R in which class functions/characters may be represented as vectors relative to conjugacy classes (e.g., R![6,-2,0,1,1]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show creating characters for Alt(5) and working with cyclotomic fields for complex values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary character operations (InnerProduct, Norm, Degree, Schur, arithmetic, tensor product)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard operations include InnerProduct(x,y) (inner product of class functions), Norm(x) (inner product of x with itself), Degree(x) (value on identity), Schur(x,k) (generalized Frobenius-Schur indicator), componentwise product, tensor product x * y, and powers x^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A character has Norm 1 iff irreducible; use InnerProduct to detect multiplicities of irreducibles in decompositions; examples illustrate removing summands by subtraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character property tests (IsCharacter, IsGeneralizedCharacter, IsIrreducible, IsLinear, IsOne, IsReal, IsFaithful, IsConjugate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions that test properties of class functions/characters: IsCharacter(x), IsGeneralizedCharacter(x), IsIrreducible(x), IsLinear(x), IsOne(x) (principal), IsReal(x), IsFaithful(x), IsConjugate(x,y) (Galois conjugates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsCharacter and IsGeneralizedCharacter require irreducible characters and will trigger creation of the character table if necessary. Use IsConjugate to check Galois conjugacy of characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacterTable(G) (Dixon-Schneider algorithm and table format)
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterTable(G) constructs the character table using the Dixon-Schneider algorithm and returns the characters as an enumerated sequence with a special printing routine. The printed table contains class descriptions (size, order), class maps for primes dividing |G|, and the characters (with Frobenius-Schur indicators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation notes: + indicates real and afforded by a real representation, - indicates real but not afforded by a real representation, 0 indicates not real. Complex character values are written in cyclotomic fields; # denotes algebraic conjugation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard character constructions (PrincipalCharacter, LinearCharacters, PermutationCharacter, PermutationGroup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convenience functions: PrincipalCharacter(G) defines the principal character; LinearCharacters(G) returns linear characters; PermutationCharacter(G, H) constructs the character from action on cosets of H; PermutationGroup(G) constructs the defining permutation character of G if G is a permutation group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to build known characters or to obtain characters from subgroup/quotient constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction, Restriction, LiftCharacter, Extension, Galois conjugation
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations for transferring characters: Induction(x, G) induces a class function from H to G; Restriction(y, H) restricts to H; LiftCharacter(x, f, G) lifts a character from a quotient via natural homomorphism f; Extension(x, f, G) is used to extend characters from a quotient; GaloisConjugate(x, j) and GaloisOrbit(x) produce Galois conjugates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Lift/Extension to obtain characters of G from characters of quotients; irreducibles of G/N correspond to irreducibles of G with N in their kernel. Galois operations require j coprime to exponent of G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition(T, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a sequence T of m characters and a character y, Decomposition(T, y) attempts to express y as y = q1*T[1] + ... + qm*T[m] + z, returning the coefficients q_i and the residue character z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically T is a list of known irreducibles; Decomposition is used to remove known irreducible summands and obtain the residue which may contain new irreducibles to be investigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor power decomposition via symmetrization and Weyl formulae (OrthogonalComponent, SymmetricComponent, OrthogonalComponents, SymplecticComponent, SymplecticComponents, Symmetrizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions implement decomposition of tensor powers χ^n into components determined by partitions of n via symmetrization and Weyl formulae. Orthogonal and symplectic variants are provided. These functions apply for n between 2 and 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to partially decompose powers χ^n into characters of smaller norm to facilitate extraction of irreducibles. Not generally useful for n>6 in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burnside (theorem) and strategy for extracting irreducibles from tensor powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Burnside's theorem: if χ is a faithful character taking t distinct values, then every irreducible character occurs as a constituent of one of χ^0, χ^1, ..., χ^{t-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical application limited by difficulty of decomposing χ^l; symmetrization and related components may give partial decompositions that help extract irreducibles.

rubrics_metrics.name: pQuotient(G, p, c) and PCGroup(G) for category transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: pQuotient(G, p, c) returns the class-c p-quotient P of G and the natural homomorphism φ : G → P. PCGroup(G) returns a polycyclic group H isomorphic to G and an isomorphism φ when G is a finite soluble permutation or matrix group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to transfer groups into categories (polycyclic) where structural computations (SNFs etc.) are more efficient; pQuotient useful when G is a finite p-group of class < c.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetAction(G, H) for permutation representation
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetAction(G, H) returns the homomorphism φ : G → T defined by action on right cosets of H, along with T and, where possible, the kernel of φ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If H is core-free (contains no nontrivial normal subgroup of G) then φ is faithful. Taking H trivial yields a faithful action but is only practical when |G| is moderate (order up to ~100000). Finding a nontrivial core-free H may be difficult unless G is well-understood.
